small_guidance:
- The elementwise epilogue is tiny; the 10.1 ms runtime is dominated by `nn.ConvTranspose3d`. Tuning BLOCK_SIZE / num_warps on `fused_kernel` will not close the gap. At most, raise BLOCK_SIZE to 4096 with num_warps=8, num_stages=2 to shave the epilogue.
- Ensure bias is broadcast via a constant `c_idx = (offsets // S) % C` only; this is already done — no further win available here.
- Real headroom is in replacing the ConvTranspose3d, not the epilogue.
large_guidance:
- Replace `nn.ConvTranspose3d` with a custom Triton scatter-add kernel: for each `(n, ic, d, h, w)` input element, scatter `x * W[ic, oc, kd, kh, kw]` into `out[n, oc, d*stride - pad + kd, ...]` using `tl.atomic_add`. Fuse the bias+residual epilogue `(2x + b)*x + x` directly into the scatter by writing into a zero-initialized buffer then doing a second elementwise pass — or, better, do the epilogue as a final fused kernel after the scatter completes.
- Alternative (likely faster on 4090): implement transposed conv as a gather-style GEMM — one program per `(N, OC tile, output-spatial tile)`, where each output voxel sums over `(ic, kd, kh, kw)` mapping back to input voxel `((od + pad - kd)/stride, ...)` valid only when the division is exact. Use BLOCK_M=64 (OC), BLOCK_N=64 (spatial), BLOCK_K=32 (IC), autotune num_warps∈{4,8}, num_stages∈{2,3}. Layout the input/weight in channels-last so the K-axis is contiguous.
- Fold the bias-add and the `(2x+b)*x + x` epilogue into the GEMM's writeback so the whole forward becomes a single kernel launch — no intermediate `out` tensor, no second pass.
